approach: Add crates/athena-core/src/context_load.rs, which measures context compression per class of work. For each class with at least 3 landed jobs it reports tokens loaded per landed job (input + cache_read + cache_write via Quantity::best_lower, summed over the invocations in JobRecords::invocations of that class's closed request jobs, divided by its landed jobs). Beside it, the same class gets the share of closed jobs that landed, the mistake count from status::mistake_report (all recorded, as the `mistakes` line counts them) and mistakes per closed job so classes of different size compare. A pure analyze() mirrors class_trend::analyze; ContextLoad::compute(&Records) feeds it. A thin class prints nothing and no qualifying class gives None, so a thin history never reads as success. Steward, audience and auditor runs are charged to no class: each gets its own generated job id (auditor.rs:338, steward.rs:1239, audience.rs:238) and is stored apart (store.rs:429-437), so no class owns it. Register the module in lib.rs, add ("context", "context_load") to STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS, add StatusView.context_load, and add display.rs `context_section(Option<&ContextLoad>) -> String` that returns "" for None. docs/spec.toml names the mechanism and ends the measure `status: context`. Tests stay inside the listed deliverables: the core integration test writes real record files and loads them with Records::load_dir (the production loader); a status.rs unit test drives the real Athena::status() over a scratch repository (code_health::tests::set_up and commit_in_tree, already used at status.rs:4283); display.rs unit tests cover the printed line and its absence. No new cli test file. The only file outside the reading's list is xtask/shard-timings.txt, with one line, because the deliverable tests/context_compression.rs is a new test target and ci_shards.rs:411-421 fails without its line.

decisions.choice: Cost is tokens loaded per LANDED job: the numerator is the tokens of all the class's closed request jobs (landed, rejected, failed, timed out); the denominator is its landed jobs. Landed share, mistakes and mistakes per closed job sit beside it.
decisions.reason: Compression that cuts tokens by losing outcomes must show up. Failed work's tokens are charged to the landed jobs, as status/throughput.rs charges time on non-landed jobs. The requirement asks for tokens beside whether outcomes held.

rejected.option: Mean tokens of landed jobs only
rejected.why: Hides the cost of failed attempts, so a cheaper class that fails more would look better.
That is the fixed per-role budget the budgets test already enforces; it says nothing about what a class of work loaded over a job.

decisions.choice: Tokens loaded = input + cache_read + cache_write, each via Quantity::best_lower() (value, else lower bound, else 0). Output tokens are excluded.
decisions.reason: Those three are what the model took in as context. A killed invocation records a lower bound and counts as the least it loaded; the line says figures are of recorded invocations.

rejected.why: Output is what the model wrote, not context loaded; it blurs the compression goal.
With prompt caching most loaded context shows as cache_read or cache_write, so input alone understates it.

decisions.choice: Answers finding 3. Tokens are read from JobRecords::invocations of each classed, closed request job (reader, producer, verifier, planner, critic). Steward, audience and auditor runs are charged to no class and the module, the tests and D175 say so. The core test includes an auditor run under its own generated-style id and asserts it is not counted, with records.auditor_runs.len() == 1 asserted so the exclusion is not vacuous.
decisions.reason: auditor.rs:338, steward.rs:1239 and audience.rs:238 give those runs a fresh RecordId::generate job id, and store.rs:429-437 puts them in steward_runs, audience_runs and auditor_runs by role. No such run ever carries a classed job's id, so Records::all_invocations() would add nothing to a per-class figure. The earlier plan's claim that it captured auditor work per class was false. The proof that the figure is exact rests on behaviors that exist: output excluded, cache tokens included, a lower-bound quantity counted at its bound, and out-of-job runs not counted.

rejected.option: Read Records::all_invocations() and attribute by job id
rejected.why: It reads the same per-job invocations plus lists no class owns; the fixture that made it look different (an auditor run carrying a job's id) is a shape production never writes.

rejected.option: Join auditor cost to the audited job through the Audit record
rejected.why: Not needed for the requirement and not a record shape this job can check on real records here; named as a follow-up in D175.

decisions.choice: Minimum of 3 landed jobs per class (MIN_LANDED_JOBS = 3). A class below it prints no line; no class qualifying gives None and the `context` line is not printed.
decisions.reason: Matches class_trend's thin-history rule (MIN_CLASS_JOBS, class_trend.rs:19) and the no-empty-success default.

rejected.option: Print every class with a 'thin' note
rejected.why: A figure from 1 or 2 jobs reads like a result.

decisions.choice: Answers finding 5. Mistakes come from status::mistake_report(records).by_class (all recorded mistakes of that class, the same source as the printed `mistakes` line). Beside the raw count the line shows mistakes per closed job (count / closed jobs). The line text says 'recorded' and D175 states the scopes: tokens, landed share and per-job rate cover closed request jobs; the raw count covers all recorded mistakes of the class, including interventions with no job.
decisions.reason: status.rs:600-602 counts by intervention class_of_work with no link to a closed job, so a raw count grows with volume. The rate makes classes comparable and the raw count keeps the two lines agreeing on what a mistake is. Intervention.job is an Option, so restricting to closed jobs would drop mistakes made by hand with no job and could disagree with the `mistakes` line.

rejected.option: Count only mistakes whose Intervention.job is a closed job of the class
rejected.why: Drops job-less interventions and would disagree with the printed `mistakes` line.
Out of scope; the accepted reading says outcomes held means landed share and mistakes.

Create crates/athena-core/src/context_load.rs. Module doc: what is counted (input + cache_read + cache_write via Quantity::best_lower, over the invocations of each classed closed request job, output excluded), what is not (steward, audience and auditor runs, which carry their own generated job ids and are charged to no class), the minimum, and that a thin history prints nothing. Define MIN_LANDED_JOBS: usize = 3, ClassJob {id, class, landed, tokens}, ClassLoad {class, closed_jobs, landed_jobs, tokens, tokens_per_landed_job, landed_percent, mistakes, mistakes_per_closed_job} and ContextLoad {classes} (derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize). analyze(&[ClassJob], &BTreeMap<String, usize>) -> Option<ContextLoad> groups by class in a BTreeMap, keeps a class only when landed jobs >= MIN_LANDED_JOBS, and fills mistakes from the map (0 if absent). ContextLoad::compute(records) takes records.request_jobs() whose state() is Closed(Landed | Rejected | Failed | TimedOut) with a class from j.class(), sums each job's own j.invocations tokens, and takes mistakes from crate::status::mistake_report(records).by_class. A closed job with no invocations is left out because it did no model work. lines() gives a header plus one line per class: `docs: 1200 tokens per landed job · 3 of 4 closed jobs landed (75%) · 2 mistake(s) recorded, 0.50 per closed job` (tokens {:.0}, percent {:.0}, rate {:.2}). Unit tests: two classes grouped, a class under the minimum dropped, no class gives None, a lower-bound quantity counts at its bound, output excluded, lines() text.
